Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second essay. The two umpires and the players have made their way out to the middle. It will be Fakhar Zaman and Abdullah Shafique to open the innings for Pakistan. David Willey is at the top of his mark and will get proceedings underway with the new ball for England. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, England have a formidable total on the board and one feels that they have their noses slightly ahead at the halfway mark. For those eternal optimists still hoping for a miracle, Pakistan will need to gun down this total in 6.4 overs to make it to the semis. Join us in a bit to see how the chase unfolds.

As he has done so often, Shaheen Afridi set the tone early for Pakistan with a first-over maiden. At the other end, Haris Rauf's horror show at the World Cup continued as he leaked 31 runs in his first three overs. It was Iftikhar Ahmed who drew first blood for Pakistan before Rauf struck in his second spell. They were not able to capitalise on the opportunity of bowling at new batters, and the dropped catch of Ben Stokes by Shaheen Afridi did them no favour. Having removed Stokes and Root in quick succession, Pakistan fought back exceptionally well, led by Haris Rauf's death-bowling masterclass. In the final over, Mohammad Wasim nailed his yorkers to help Pakistan finish strongly with the ball.

After Jos Buttler won the flip of the coin, he had no hesitation in electing to put runs on the board. It was a solid start for England as Jonny Bairstow and Dawid Malan saw through the difficult phase successfully to stitch an 82-run opening stand. Malan departed on 31, but Bairstow notched up his second fifty of this World Cup before being dismissed on 59. Joe Root and Ben Stokes then got together and took the innings forward on a surface that was not easy for the incoming batter. Stokes, the aggressor of the two batters, fell 16 runs short of his hundred, while Root, who had struggled for fluency for most of his innings, got out on 60. Jos Buttler and Harry Brook had full licence to tee off from ball one, and they sure did, chipping in with handy cameos. Playing in his last game for England, David Willey struck a few lusty blows in the final over to take England over 335.

An eventful end to the innings, and England finish with 337 on the board! At one stage in the game, they were well-placed to go over 350 but they will be fairly pleased with this total. As for Pakistan, their slim chance of making it through to the next stage diminished as soon as the flip of the coin landed in Jos Buttler's favour and he opted to bat first. Nonetheless, they have fought back well with the ball to limit England to a chasable total.

We are at match number 44 of the ICC Cricket World Cup 2023 where England go up against Pakistan at Eden Gardens in Kolkata. This match is a very important one for England as their qualification for the 2025 Champion's Trophy hangs in the balance. They have had a campaign to forget as they have lost 6 out of the 8 matches so far. They must have gained some confidence after winning their last game against the Netherlands quite comfortably. Their batting unit regained their form with Dawid Malan scoring at a good rate. After Jonny Bairstow, Joe Root, and Harry Brook were dismissed it was again Ben Stokes who rescued them from a collapse. He scored a fine century and kept the scoreboard going. Chris Woakes supported him down the order and ensured that the English put up a good total on the board.  In the bowing unit, the spinners, Adil Rashid and Moeen Ali rose to the occasion and took 3 wickets each. David Willey and Chris Woakes were very economical in the early overs and even took a few wickets. It was a good performance by England but they will have to work on a few things for their match against Pakistan. They will hope to win this one and end the tournament on a good note also moving up a few places on the points table will mean that they will have qualified for the Champion's Trophy. Pakistan on the other hand will be playing this match to end their tournament with a win. Their chances of qualifying for the semi-finals are next to impossible with the current scenario. To qualify Pakistan will have to beat England by a margin of more than 287 runs or chase the target with 284 balls to spare. Pakistan have had a rough middle patch of the tournament and despite a strong start, they could not finish in the top 4. However, they showed their strength in their last game against the Kiwis. They had to chase 402 on the board with the target of improving their NRR. The bowlers failed to take timely wickets but Mohammad Wasim shone out as he scalped 3. It was a rain-affected match but Fakhar Zaman and Babar Azam made sure that they stayed well over the DLS score. Unfortunately for the Kiwis, the rain stopped the match and Pakistan clinched an important win. With Fakhar Zaman in form and back in the side, their batting order looks much stronger. Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan are dangerous in the middle order with Iftikhar Ahmed and Saud Shakeel to provide a strong finish. Their pace attack hasn't been very effective in these conditions, especially with Haris Rauf not being able to take wickets. Mohammad Wasim looks in good rhythm which will help Shaheen Afridi to bowl freely. This is expected to be an exciting clash where both teams will look to end their tournament with a win.
